name: Plansee
kurzbeschreibung: Lake Plansee near Reutte is Tirol's second-largest lake—a fjord-like alpine wonderland boasting emerald water, scenic passenger cruises, and pebble beaches.
preis: Free public shoreline access (parking fees apply approx. 5–8 €; passenger ferry charges fares)
oeffnungszeiten: Accessible year-round; passenger boats and water sports operate May to October
beschreibung:
Überblick

Lake Plansee, set at an elevation of 976 metres amidst the rugged limestone crags of the Ammergau Alps in the Außerfern district, constitutes Tirol's second-largest natural lake with a surface area of 2.8 square kilometres and depths plunging to 78 metres. Connected via a scenic 300-metre canal to adjoining Lake Heiterwang, this aquatic pair forms a dramatic fjord-like mountain waterway unique in the Eastern Alps. Renowned for outstanding Grade I drinking-water purity and luminous emerald-to-sapphire hues, Plansee draws wild swimmers, divers, stand-up paddleboarders, and sailing enthusiasts from afar. Forested slopes and pale limestone bluffs descend steeply into transparent waters, bordered by natural gravel coves and sunny meadows harboring abundant trout, char, and whitefish.

Route & Anforderungen

Recreation at Lake Plansee accommodates leisurely family rambles and rigorous alpine expeditions alike. A classic shoreline hiking trail hugs the water, which can be linked with Lake Heiterwang to form an exhilarating 20-kilometre full circuit (approx. 5 to 6 hours walking time, easy-to-moderate grade T1–T2). Numerous secluded pebble beaches offer peaceful swimming stops. Mountaineers can tackle demanding climbs up the craggy Geierköpfe peaks rising directly above the southern bank. Sturdy walking shoes with reliable tread are recommended for undulating shoreline paths. Families particularly cherish combining a scenic lakeside walk with a return ride aboard the historical passenger ferry fleet.

Besuch & Anreise

Access from Reutte is via Breitenwang along provincial road L255, which traces the northern shore before connecting onwards toward Ettal and Linderhof Palace in Bavaria. By public transit, rail travelers alight at Reutte in Tirol station and board summer hiker shuttles directly to lakeside stops. Multiple organized pay-and-display parking lots are situated along the northern road.

Tipps

Board the vintage motor passenger ships MS Margarethe or MS Willi for an unforgettable cruise gliding between Plansee and Heiterwanger See. Stand-up paddleboarders should launch in early morning calm when glassy reflections mimic the towering limestone walls.
